xmldoc.short_description: Return calendar durations between two datetime values.

param_input_item.param_description: Two datetime or date-compatible inputs and an optional component selector such as years, quarters, months, or days.

description.p: Return calendar durations between two datetime values.

components is one name or a cell of names among 'years', 'quarters', 'months', 'weeks', 'days' and 'time' (default: years, months, days and time). Only those components are used, from the largest to the smallest: each one takes the most whole units that do not go past t2, the rest goes to the next one. So t1 + c is t2 when 'time' is asked, except with 'quarters' when some whole months are left over: those months are added then removed again, which can move a month-end day (31 January becomes 29 January in 2024), and the next components start from that day. When the time of day of t2 is earlier than the one of t1, the last day is not counted and the time part holds the hours left.

The Format of the result follows the components: 'ymdt' by default, 'mdt' without years, with 'q' for quarters and 'w' for weeks. The time part of zoned datetimes is the elapsed time. A NaT gives NaN.
Array-valued inputs keep their data shape when the operation supports arrays. Scalar operands are expanded where the implementation defines scalar expansion.

example_item.example_item_data: c = between(datetime(2024, 1, 15), datetime(2024, 3, 20)) split(c, 'months') split(c, 'days') between(datetime(2024, 1, 31, 12, 0, 0), datetime(2024, 4, 1, 6, 0, 0)) between(datetime(2024, 1, 31, 12, 0, 0), datetime(2024, 4, 1, 6, 0, 0), {'weeks', 'days'})

example_item.example_item_description: Quarters: the months left over are stepped back, so a month-end start day can move.
